details:
**Murder of Osiris**
Set's most famous act. Jealous of his brother Osiris, king of Egypt, he tricked Osiris into lying down in a custom-made chest (coffin), sealed it, and threw it into the Nile. When Isis recovered the body, Set cut it into 14 pieces and scattered them across Egypt, then took the throne.

**Stone boat race**
One of the contests between Set and his nephew Horus. They agreed to race boats made of stone. Horus secretly built a wooden boat and plastered it to look like stone, while Set built a real stone boat that sank, so he lost.

**Defeating Apep (Apophis)**
Set rode on the prow of the sun god Ra's solar barge during its nightly journey through the underworld and speared the chaos serpent Apep, which tried to swallow the sun each night. This role made him a protector of Ra despite his villainy elsewhere.

**The Contendings of Horus and Seth**
A New Kingdom text describing the 80-year struggle between Set and Horus, Osiris's son, for the throne of Egypt before a tribunal of gods. Its episodes include the boat race, the lettuce trick, and Set gouging out Horus's eye.

**Lettuce and semen**
In the Contendings, Set tried to humiliate Horus by sexually dominating him, but Horus caught Set's semen. Isis then spread Horus's semen on lettuce, Set's favorite food (said to be the only thing he ate), and when the gods summoned the semen, it answered from inside Set, shaming him before the tribunal.

**Horus's eye and Set's testicles**
In their fights, Set tore out Horus's eye, which was later restored and became the Eye of Horus, a symbol of healing and protection. Horus in turn tore off Set's testicles, which was said to explain the barrenness of Set's desert domain.

**Nephthys and Anubis**
Set's wife and sister. She disguised herself as her sister Isis and slept with Osiris, conceiving Anubis, which angered Set.

**God of the "Red Land" and foreigners**
When Geb divided Egypt, he gave the fertile black land of the Nile valley to Horus and the barren desert, the "red land" (deshret), to Set. Set was also the god of storms, chaos, violence, and foreign lands.

**Hyksos worship at Avaris**
The Hyksos, foreign rulers of northern Egypt, made Set their chief god at their capital Avaris and identified him with the Canaanite storm god Baal. The Hyksos king Apepi was a devotee. The later 400 Year Stela commemorated the 400th anniversary of Set's cult there.

**Ombos (Nubt)**
Set's main cult center in Upper Egypt, near Naqada. He was called "the Ombite" ("he of Nubt"), and some of the earliest images of the Set animal date to the Naqada period.

**Isis's trick**
In the Contendings, Isis disguised herself as a widow and told Set that a stranger had stolen her son's inheritance. When Set said this was wrong, he condemned himself, since he had stolen Horus's inheritance.

**Anat and Astarte**
To settle the dispute, the goddess Neith advised that Horus receive the throne and that Set be compensated with two foreign goddesses, the Canaanite Anat and Astarte, as wives.

**Typhon**
Greek writers, especially Plutarch in On Isis and Osiris, identified Set with Typhon, the monstrous enemy of Zeus.

**The Set animal and was scepter**
Set is depicted with the head of an unidentified creature with a long curved snout and tall flat-topped ears, sometimes with a forked tail. He often holds the was scepter, a staff topped with the head of a similar animal. He was also associated with pigs, hippos, and donkeys.
